question: Under Leibniz's rule (names that agree at every radius are one place), does every one of the 1,024 Life-like one-bit laws and the atom either have finitely many solutions on the tree (every board finite) or have a periodic solution using a branching pattern (so, by Lemma A, the tree and an infinite board with cyclic stabilizer are boards)?

definitions.the family: As in BOARD-DIST-20261110-001B: the 1,024 Life-like laws (key L<m>) and the atom x, y -> c; controls: the full law and the empty law.
definitions.tree patterns: board_lib.tree_patterns: the patterns of places in solutions on the tree (the greatest fixpoint of half-tree pattern sets).
definitions.branching pattern: A tree pattern p with at least two patterns q in the half-tree set H[h] compatible with p in some direction h: the h-neighbour's half-tree has two completions.
definitions.periodic solution: A colouring of a finite board (a transitive pair of permutations) with every pattern allowed; it lifts to a solution on the tree with finite orbit.
definitions.classes: E: no tree pattern. D: tree patterns, none branching (every solution is fixed by its pattern at one name, so there are finitely many and every board is finite). A: some periodic solution on a finite board with at most 6 places, or at most 8 for the laws not yet decided, uses a branching pattern. U: branching, and no such periodic solution found.
definitions.plane reading (class A): Some solution on a torus Z^2/Lambda of index at most 16 has a cell or a 2 x 2 block that can be refilled differently with every pattern still allowed: then independent refills at sparse translates give aperiodic solutions on the plane, so the plane is a board. Otherwise not decided.

public_inputs.code: census.py (sha256 ebdd25b1ed6c99a63f384ee1755d6664e77499358232ae92e65a6e67c56ff699) beside this file, importing board_lib.py of BOARD-DIST-20261110-001B-E001 (sha256 72a52aafee769792d1c0eb4ca5c7a2e1d4d446876994fee6b20875f660132458); numpy.

forbidden_inputs: Changing the family, the classes, the board bounds (6, then 8 places), the torus bound (16) or the prediction after seeing results
primary_observable: Each law's class, its periodic branching board when in A, and the plane reading.
cheapest_meaningful_control: The full law (class A) and the empty law (class E), run first; smoke-tested before freezing on boards to 3 places (disclosed). No law of the family was run.

predictions.C1: No law of the family is in class U: every Life-like law and the atom is in E, D or A.
predictions.C2: The full law is in A and the empty law in E.

decision_rules.C1 holds: For every law of the family W and P hold (T3 and T6 of ticket A), and S fails for every law in class A.
decision_rules.C1 fails: Each law in U is reported and examined by hand as a candidate against W; U alone is not a refutation, since it only means the census did not decide.
decision_rules.plane reading: Reported as a count; laws in A without a certificate are listed, not decided.

stop_rule: One run on the frozen family; no rerun with changed bounds.
runtime: Expected minutes; registered in docs/LONG_RUNNING.md before launch if expected past ten minutes, and run under systemd-run MemoryMax=16G with no swap.
revision_before_run: 2026-11-10, before any run of the family: census.py's plane reading was vectorized and now checks every solution on each torus, as the definition says (the first version checked one solution per torus and would have taken hours); the classes, bounds, prediction and decision rules are unchanged.
